text: {"distance_m": 2, "reasoning_short": "Seeing a small low-contrast spot is a detection limit, not 20/20 resolution. For tiny targets, threshold depends roughly on contrast times area (Riccò-type summation). From Blackwell-type data, a 1 arcmin spot needs about 30–40% contrast, so at 15% contrast the spot must subtend roughly 1.5–2 arcmin. A 1 mm spot at about 1.7 arcmin (≈5e-4 rad) is about 2 m away. This is an approximate estimate."}
